text: Hello, and welcome. In this video you will see the new Packaging module in Ironline. It finds the cheapest way to pack and ship each part: which box, tote or crate, how many parts go in it, how many boxes fit on a pallet, how many pallets fit in the truck, and what all of that costs per part.

Open Supply, then Packaging. Everything happens on one screen: settings on the left, a large 3D workspace in the middle, and the packing options on the right. Choose the part, here the drive hub, D M W ten forty.

Ironline needs the part's size and weight. The part already has a 3D model, so click Measure from the 3D model, and the length, width and height are filled in for you. Then type the weight of one part, here one point two kilograms.

Straight away, every container, pallet and truck you selected is counted and costed. The options on the right are ranked with the cheapest cost per part at the top. Each card shows the parts per container, per pallet and per truck, and a note when the lifting weight or the pallet limits the count.

The icons on the left switch between the settings. Packing chooses how parts go in: flat layers turns each part whichever way fits the most, one per cell gives every part its own cell with dividers, and nested stacks is for parts that slide into each other. You can also set the clearance around each part, pads between layers, and the most a person should lift.

Click any option to see it in the 3D workspace. This is the inside of the container. Slide Spread layers to pull the layers apart. Then switch to the pallet, and to the truck, to see the whole load. Drag to turn the view.

Under the options is the cost per part, split into the container, pads and dividers, the pallet and wrap, and the freight, with the packing instruction. The Shipping tab prices freight per pallet or per truck, and you can enter a real shipment, for example five hundred parts, to see what that order costs to ship.

Now the clever part. Click Find best carton size. Ironline designs cartons built exactly around whole numbers of parts, chooses the cheapest cardboard grade that is still strong enough for the pallet stack, and adds the best five to the list. Here a made to size carton is much cheaper per part than any stock box.

The Payback tab compares returnable totes with throw away cartons. Enter the parts per year and how many days a tote is away, and you see the fleet you need, what it costs, the yearly saving, and the payback time. Here the made to size carton is so cheap that the totes would never pay back, so the carton wins.

When you are happy, click Use for part. The packing is saved on the part. The Report button prints a one page packing report with the 3D picture, the counts and the costs, ready to send to a customer.

The part page now has a Packing tab with the saved packing. And every job for this part shows the packing instruction, and how many containers that job needs, so the shop floor knows exactly how to pack it.
Finally, the Library tab holds your own cartons, totes, crates, pallets and trucks, with their sizes, weights, prices and limits. Click Add to put in your own, or click any line to change it.
That is Packaging in Ironline: pick the part, compare the options, find the best carton, and save it for the shop floor. Thank you for watching.
